They keep mailing out all these ads to sign up for Fiber, and its really annoying because it is impossible to find a serviceable address! I'm fairly certain they are over touting their Fiber service to combat all the Google Fiber news, but they have to have service somewhere, right?
Century Link Fiber - Anyone have information, or know where it can be found, regarding their actual service area?

They came to my door and wanted me to sign up for century "fiber". After asking some questions I found out they ran fiber to some central location somewhere and the signal will come to my house via the phone wires, with a max speed of 20mbps. Their campaign seems a little phony to me.
I would have asked them how that differs from DSL at all. Sounds like a rebranding of the same exact service.

I am on their fiber plan! Currently, I am going the cheap route and have 40Mbps / 20Mbps for $30/month. Their 1Gbps plan is $130 or so. :(

As far as availability, call them up. They can quickly tell you based on your address. I am located in the 1100 E 1700 S area.

To answer captbrogers, it differs from DSL in that it is NOT over a phone line. They ran a fiber-optic line straight to my house and into a converter box that converts the signal to electricity (ethernet) which runs into my office.

Side-story: The box that converts the fiber signal to Ethernet has a battery backup. I had mine placed on the wall behind my fridge. Well, a jug of water on top of the fridge leaked, soaking the battery backup. I dried it out, but the battery was toast. I called in, and the tech said: "Well, normally we'd charge for those ... it would be a shame if one just happened to end up on your back porch." I came home from work, and voila! A brand-new battery AND the control box were sitting on my back porch. I've never worked with such cool technicians.
